rule: a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). | locals, parameters, fields, and file-scope globals/statics (C, C++, ObjC, Zig, Rust `static`). | A type alias (`using X = T;`, `typedef T X;`, Zig `const X = a.b.T`) is expanded to its target | Generic/template type arguments are dropped from every ID (`HashSet#<init>`). | Dot-syntax property access is not a call.
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. Receivers typed by declarations: parameter `param`, ivar `_spare` (field), property `self.engine` (`obj.field` chain whose property has a declared type; the dot access itself is not a call), file-scope static `gEngine` (Decision 2026-10-29), typedef alias `MotorAlias` expanded to `Engine`, for-in loop variable `each`, catch parameter `e` (NSException, external → medium). `NSArray<Engine *>`: lightweight-generic arguments dropped → `NSArray#count`, medium (external type). Message syntax `[e reason]` is a call even though `reason` is a property; only dot syntax is exempt.
